maria: Heads up — while running the long-context perf sweep I hit a regression in the prefill-heavy mixes. Baseline (v1.2.0) -> v1.3.0 shows ~+28% median latency and p99 tokens/s drop. Any ideas?

samir: I noticed that too. Quick profiler shows the kernel picker is choosing GEMM_QUANT8 much more for the 32k sequences than before. That seems suspicious.

elaine: Can you paste the profiler dump? small snippets are fine. Also which batcher config?

maria: Batcher=continuous, batch_size target 8, concurrency 16. Repro command I used locally: 
```
tools/replay --profile --seed=2026 --dist "prefill:0.8,short:0.15,long:0.05" --max-seq 32768 --kv-hit 0.45 --batcher continuous --concurrency 16
```
Used the same model binary as CI.

perf-bot: Perf-summary: run_id=2026-175000, scenario=prefill-heavy-32k, batcher=continuous, target_batch=8, concurrency=16, kv_hit=0.45. Observed: avg_latency +26%, p99_tokens/s -30%. Kernel selection breakdown: GEMM_QUANT8 47%, FLASH_ATTENTION_F16 31%, FALLBACKS (slow kernels) 22%.

jon: That % fallback looks high. Could be the kernel selector updated its cost model for large sequence prefill (prefill dominates ops) and now prefers quant kernels that are faster on decode but expensive on big prefill mats.

samir: Exactly — the selector uses an estimated cost = alpha * prefill_ops + (1-alpha) * decode_ops. If alpha got reduced in the last change, it would underweight prefill cost and pick kernels optimized for decode. For long prefill mixes that is bad.

elaine: Also, KV cache behavior matters. If the replay harness doesn't warm the KV cache properly we may be measuring repeated full prefill passes which amplify kernel differences. Maria, what's the measured KV hit curve over time?

maria: KV hit started ~0.2 and ramps to ~0.6 after ~10 requests in that run. But because prefill is 80% of requests, many requests are full prefill so median treat as low-hit.

samir: Repro tip: run two passes. 1) warmup phase with tuned kv-hit=0.9 to populate cache, 2) measurement phase with the target distribution. Otherwise the mixing confounds kernel choice.

elaine: Paste of a small profiler flame (cropped):
```
[profiler] top functions by time:
  - attention_forward (FLASH) : 32%
  - gemm_quant8_matmul        : 29%
  - kv_cache_apply            : 18%
  - alloc/pinning             : 11%
  - scheduler overhead        : 10%
```
Note: the FLASH percent is from decode paths; GEMM_QUANT8 during prefill spikes memory bandwidth.

jon: For apples-to-apples we should fix: hardware (same host), same model binary, same runtime flags, and an explicit warmup. Also match sequence length distribution exactly and report KV hit curve.

maria: Agreed. Proposal for a deterministic harness invocation to share in perf repo: 
```
tools/replay --scenario prefill-heavy-longcontext \
  --seed 2026 \
  --warmup-requests 50 \
  --dist "prefill:0.8,short:0.15,long:0.05" \
  --max-seq 32768 \
  --kv-target 0.6 \
  --batcher continuous \
  --target-batch 8 \
  --concurrency 16 \
  --capture-kv-curve /tmp/kv_curve.csv \
  --profile out/2026-profile.json
```
This should make comparisons reproducible.

samir: Also add flags to pin kernel-selector weights: `--ks-alpha N` so we can force alpha to previous value and compare. For experimentation I ran with `--ks-alpha 0.85` (old value) and perf reverted to baseline numbers.

elaine: Good scientific test. Two experiments: (A) current selector, (B) forced alpha=0.85. Keep everything else identical. Collect kernel selection logs.

perf-bot: Created ticket RINF-1324: "prefill-heavy longcontext regression - kernel selector tuning & harness". link: https://redwood.atlassian.example/browse/RINF-1324

jon: Action items: samir will add the `prefill-heavy-longcontext` scenario + ks-alpha flag to tools/replay. elaine will add a CI perf job (nightly) that runs the scenario on a stable host image. maria will run local gated comparisons and paste results.

samir: I'll also add a small synthetic micro-benchmark that isolates prefill matrix sizes to validate kernel cost curves (no kv, no batching) so we can see where GEMM_QUANT8 wins vs FLASH.

maria: I'll run the two-run comparison tonight and paste a short table in the thread. If we see alpha fix restores perf then we know it's selector tuning; if not, we dig deeper into memory alloc patterns.

ci-bot: CI job queued: perf/prefill-heavy-longcontext/nightly on hw-tag=gpu-a100-80gb image=runtime-stable. Job link: https://ci.redwood.example/job/4582

elaine: One more note — when reporting put sequence-length histogram and prefill token ratio. Long-context numbers are very sensitive to tail seqs. Also include the bucketed batch-size distribution so we can check batching heuristics.

maria: Will do. Thanks all — I'll update after the runs.

samir: Thanks, keeping this thread for results and kernel logs only. Please avoid dumping unrelated build logs here.
